A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TCP benchmark. Their main text, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original LLM evaluations on TCP, human validation, prototype experiments and analyses of model errors.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds an experiment supplying temporal knowledge to three reasoning models.

M1.justification: Prototype generation, exhaustive-search labeling, scenario generation, concretization and hard/soft verification remain unchanged. The added knowledge-supplied experiment is a diagnostic condition, not a revision of the benchmark construction method.

E1.justification: Appendix G adds an evaluation scenario in which temporal facts are supplied, changing the information available to models. The underlying TCP coverage remains 600 short/long problems across ten domains; Figure 19 illustrates existing problem categories.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged, including all models and prompting variants in Tables 3–5. The added knowledge experiment uses the same three reasoning models already compared in the prototype analysis.

E3.justification: The new experiment supplements long-problem prompts with the relevant weekday and short-problem prompts with relative time-zone differences. Previously reported benchmark settings and accuracy evaluation remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish rerunning the original experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix G and new Table 6 test whether supplying temporal factual knowledge alleviates planning failures. Existing dependency, domain, output-length, time-zone, prototype and qualitative case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix D removes the reasoning-length comparison's t-test statistics, t = 3.50 and p = 0.0008, while retaining its means and 'statistically significant' wording. The stated three-run averaging practice for reasoning models is unchanged.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports knowledge-supplied overall accuracies of 60.45, 71.64 and 69.34 for Gemini 2.5 Flash, Gemini 2.5 Pro and o4-mini. Tables 3–5 retain their scores. Section 4.2 corrects the previously swapped attribution of 81.39 to o4-mini and 71.37 to Gemini 2.5 Pro.

T1.justification: The dependency patterns and mathematical content remain unchanged. Table 2 corrects its prose to agree with the existing A→B→C pattern; neither version presents formal theorems or proofs, and Appendix G adds conceptual discussion rather than formal theory.

C1.justification: TCP's claimed novelty, joint temporal-reasoning/planning purpose and headline findings retain their scope. The abstract adds 'may' before 'struggle,' but the introduction and conclusion retain the same substantive claims.

C2.justification: Appendix G introduces temporal reasoning as either an independent capability or a combination of knowledge and reasoning. It attributes the limited benefit of supplied facts to interacting constraints, although Table 6 shows mixed changes rather than uniformly lower accuracy. Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Hardware, software, precise model identifiers, access links, annotation instructions and construction/verification prompts are retained. The existing prompts move from Appendix G to H without substantive changes.

R1.justification: Related work adds Saxena et al. (2021) and Ding et al. (2023) on temporal knowledge-graph QA, and Zhang et al. (2024) and Wu et al. (2025) on multitask planning. These extend the discussion without redefining TCP's overall positioning.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized grammatical and terminology corrections, including TCSP to TCP and Table 2's self-dependency typo. It adds acknowledgements and two appendix sections while preserving the main narrative and section organization.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 6 and Figure 19, supplies answers and a longer caption in Figure 1, and redraws Figures 1 and 3 with red highlighting. Existing appendix displays are relocated or renumbered. Appendix I's descriptions reverse the dependency patterns shown in Figure 19's bottom examples.

improvement.justification: The knowledge-control experiment and corrected score attribution provide useful gains. However, v2 removes statistical evidence while retaining the significance claim and introduces misleading example documentation: Figure 1's new long-example answer conflicts with its sequential 1-, 2- and 3-day tasks, and Appendix I mismatches Figure 19's dependency patterns. These benefits and reporting defects leave the net quality direction uncertain.
